title: QBR Compass: Adoption & Renewal Playbook (Dual-Track: Standard + Enterprise)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a modular QBR deck template and renewal playbook for Customer Success managers running quarterly business reviews. It supports a dual-track delivery: a condensed Standard QBR for smaller customers (30–45 minutes) and an expanded Enterprise QBR for strategic accounts (60–90 minutes). Use slide modules to compose the meeting based on account tier, maturity, and renewal risk.

How to use this file:
- Pick the track (Standard or Enterprise).
- Replace bracketed placeholders with account-specific data.
- Attach the Renewal Tracker export (CSV) and any recent support/sales sync notes.
- Run the 10-minute internal pre-brief with Sales/Systems/AE to align asks and owners.

Deck architecture (modular blocks and timing):
1) Title + Logistics (1 slide, 1 min)
- Slide elements: Customer logo, date, attendees (roles + escalation contacts), meeting objective
- Speaker note: Keep expectations explicit; one-sentence meeting outcome (e.g., "Align on renewal commitment and 90-day adoption milestones").

2) Executive snapshot (1 slide, 3 min)
- Elements: Executive summary of value delivered, NRR direction, top success metric vs. committed goal
- Standard track: 1 KPI and headline statement
- Enterprise track: 2–3 KPIs + short customer quote or ROI callout

3) Usage and adoption heatmap (1–2 slides, 8 min)
- Visual: month-over-month active routes, tokens per session, embedding calls, top 5 endpoints by volume
- Adoption flags: Feature adoption (console, SDK, dedicated capacity), churn signals, API error trends
- Speaker note: Highlight anomalies and causal hypotheses (e.g., rollout of new feature X increased embedding volume by 32%).

4) Value realized vs. contract (1 slide, 5 min)
- Metrics: Estimated cost savings, latency improvements, throughput gains, time-to-answer or productized KPI impact
- Enterprise variant: Include a modeled ROI table for 6/12/24 months with conservative/expected/upside scenarios.

5) Open technical and operational risks (1 slide, 5–10 min)
- Template sections: Incident history since last QBR, unresolved tickets older than 14 days, capacity/latency risks, compliance items (if applicable)
- Enterprise add-on: Runbook readiness, DR test cadence, audit artifact status.

6) Renewal readiness and ask (1 slide, 5 min)
- Elements: Renewal date, current ARR, renewal target (yes/no/pending), blocker matrix (commercial, technical, budget, exec alignment)
- Suggested asks per tier:
  - Standard: Request a letter of intent or 12-month renewal via AE; confirm next steps and billing contact.
  - Enterprise: Schedule a renewal readiness workshop within 14 days; propose contract term and SLO against latency/uptime.

7) Roadmap & partnership opportunities (1–2 slides, 7–10 min)
- Elements: Product features that map to customer use cases, proposed pilot/workshop, integration suggestions
- Enterprise variant: Co-sell motion, executive sponsor nomination, strategic milestones and success criteria.

8) Renewal tracker snapshot (1 slide, 3–5 min)
- Mini-table: Renewal window, ARR at risk, probability, next action owner, target close date
- Use the following columns in your export: Account, Renewal Date, ARR, Risk Level (Low/Med/High), Probability %, AE Owner, CS Owner, Next Action, Last Contact Date

9) Action plan and owners (1 slide, 3 min)
- 30/60/90 day commitments with owner and measurable outcomes
- Escalation path and decision criteria

10) Appendix: Data sources and artifacts (variable)
- Linked artifacts: recent support tickets, audit logs, performance traces, billing snapshot, reference Confluence pages

Slide text templates and placeholders (copy into deck):
- Title slide: "Quarterly Business Review — [Customer Name] — [YYYY-MM-DD]"
- Executive snapshot headline: "In the last 90 days: [Key outcome: e.g., 21% reduction in inference latency; 3x throughput on dedicated pool]."
- Usage headline: "Active routes up/down by [X%]; top endpoints: [list]."
- Renewal ask copy (Standard): "We recommend moving to a 12-month renewal at $[ARR]. Next step: AE to send renewal term sheet by [date]."
- Renewal ask copy (Enterprise): "Propose a strategic renewal with custom SLA and a [X]% committed capacity pool. Request executive alignment session by [date]."

Speaker cues and facilitation tips:
- Pre-brief (10 min): Confirm if there are any sensitive commercial negotiations in flight; adjust ask language accordingly.
- Keep Executive snapshot factual and quantified; avoid product-session deep dives unless requested.
- When presenting risks, pair each risk with a mitigation or owner.

Custom reuse patterns and recipes (examples):
- High-risk Renewal Rescue (short checklist): escalate to AE+Head of CS, book a technical deep-dive within 7 days, provide interim runbook for immediate mitigation, propose a short-term credit or NFR pilot to preserve relationship.
- Expansion Play (low risk): introduce Enterprise roadmap module, propose a pilot for Optimize toolkit, co-sell collateral for procurement.

Quick renewal tracker (text table you can paste into a sheet):
Account | Renewal Date | ARR | Risk | Prob% | AE | CS | Next Action | Target Close
[Acme Corp] | 2026-03-30 | $120,000 | High | 40 | Jordan Li | Alyssa Chen | Exec meeting scheduled 2026-03-10 | 2026-03-30
[BetaApps] | 2026-05-12 | $18,000 | Low | 85 | Priya Nair | Marco Reyes | AE to send PO reminder 2026-04-15 | 2026-05-12

Meeting length guidance and attendee recommendations:
- Standard (30–45m): CS Manager, AE, Engineering SME (optional), Billing or Procurement owner (if near renewal)
- Enterprise (60–90m): CS Director, AE, Solutions Engineer, Product (roadmap), Finance/Procurement, Customer exec sponsor

Templates for follow-up emails (paste-ready):
- Standard follow-up: "Thanks for your time today. Recap: [3 bullets]. Next step: AE to send renewal term sheet by [date]."
- Enterprise follow-up: "Thanks — we agreed on [3 top commitments]. Attached: draft SOW, proposed SLA, and proposed executive alignment meeting agenda for [date]."

Checklist before sending to customer:
- Data validation: confirm last 90-day usage and billing figures
- Internal alignment: last 10-minute pre-brief completed and owner roster confirmed
- Attachments: Renewal tracker CSV, incident postmortems (if discussed), proposed SOW or term sheet (if applicable)

Common pitfalls and remediation suggestions:
- Pitfall: Presenting too many metrics — keep the executive snapshot to 2–3 KPIs.
- Pitfall: No explicit ask — every QBR must close with a clear next step and owner.
- Pitfall: Technical debt hidden in tickets — surface tickets older than 14 days and assign a remediation sprint.

Appendix: Sample 90-day action plan (paste into slide)
- Day 0–14: Executive alignment meeting, confirm renewal ask, patch critical tickets
- Day 15–45: Run performance tuning session, pilot Optimize recommendations, complete cost-of-ownership analysis
- Day 46–90: Billing & contract negotiations, final sign-off, onboarding of new footprint (if expanded)

Notes to CS:
- Customize the Enterprise ROI model conservatively; include a mid-case and downside case for finance.
- Keep the Renewal Tracker single-source-of-truth in the shared spreadsheet and update it after every customer touch.

Version history and review:
- v0.1 2025-11-01: initial draft (Alyssa)
- v0.4 2026-01-20: added Enterprise ROI module (Priya)
- v0.7 2026-02-10: included high-risk rescue flow (Marco)
- v1.0 planned: Post pilot with Sales feedback

End of document.
